record.field: Collectors record what customers pay them, see what they hold in custody and hand it in through their own remittances.
Privilege: a collector records the payment a customer handed them

A collector who holds no accounting right records a customer's payment in a collection custody journal: creating and posting that payment and its entry in their own name, reading the customer's open posted invoices and reconciling them with it. Nothing else of accounting is theirs.
Privilege: whoever acts on a collector's work reads what that collector holds

Whether a collector holds collections past their hand-in date, or above their limit, decides what they may do next: collect more, or have a credit sale confirmed. Whoever asks reads the collector's collections in custody journals, and nothing else of their payments.
